title: Use of a PHILOS Plate for Fixation of a Pathological Subtrochanteric Fracture Secondary to an Aneurysmal Bone Cyst in a Child: A Case Report أستخدام شريحة فيلوس لتثبيت كسر مرضي ثانوي نتيجة كيس دموي حميدي تحت المدورين لعظمة الفخذ لدى طفل : تقرير حاله
journal: Derna Academy Journal for Applied Sciences
abstract: يُعدّ الكيس العظمي الدموي آفة عظمية نادرة، حميدة، لكنها قد تكون موضعياً عدوانية، وتصيب غالباً الأطفال والمراهقين. ويتطلب حدوث كسر مرضي في منطقة أعلى عظم الفخذ نتيجة هذه الآفة معالجة الكيس وتحقيق تثبيت مستقر للكسر في الوقت نفسه. حضر طفل يبلغ من العمر 9 سنوات إلى مركز طبرق الطبي في ليبيا بعد تعرضه لإصابة بسيطة، وكان يعاني من ألم وضعف في وظيفة الطرف السفلي الأيمن. أظهرت الصور الشعاعية وجود كسر مرضي تحت المدور عبر آفة حالّة للعظم في الجزء القريب من عظم الفخذ. وأكد الفحص النسيجي لعينة مأخوذة أثناء العملية تشخيص الكيس العظمي الدموي. وبعد معالجة الآفة، ثُبّت الكسر باستخدام صفيحة نظام التثبيت الداخلي خاصه للطرف القريب من عظم العضد ولكنها استخدمت للفخذ ، وذلك يعتبر خارج الاستطباب الأصلي للصفيحة. حدث في الفترة المبكرة بعد العملية تباعد في حواف الجرح، وأظهرت المزرعة نمو بكتيريا المكورات العنقودية الذهبية ، وقد تحسنت الحالة بعد إعطاء مضاد حيوي وفق نتائج المزرعة واختبار الحساسية. وفي آخر متابعة موثقة، كانت الحالة السريرية للطفل جيدة مع محاذاة مرضية للكسر. ويمكن أن تمثل صفيحة خياراً بديلاً للتثبيت في حالات مختارة من الكسور المرضية في الجزء القريب من عظم الفخذ لدى الأطفال، مع ضرورة المتابعة لمدة أطول لتقييم الالتئام، واحتمال عودة الكيس، وسلامة صفيحة النمو.

title: TikTok como herramienta de educación sexual en adolescentes: beneficios, riesgos y estrategias de prevención desde enfermería. Revisión de literatura (2020–2026)
abstract: TikTok se ha consolidado como una fuente accesible de información sobre sexualidad entre adolescentes, aunque sus contenidos pueden combinar orientación útil, experiencias personales y desinformación. El objetivo fue analizar beneficios, riesgos y posibilidades de prevención desde enfermería asociados con su uso para educación sexual adolescente. Se desarrolló una revisión integrativa mediante el análisis de un archivo CSV exportado de Scopus, con una ventana de interés de 2020 a 2026. De 51 registros examinados, se seleccionaron 31 publicaciones: 21 de pertinencia temática directa y diez de contexto complementario. La síntesis identificó oportunidades para ampliar conversaciones sobre menstruación, anticoncepción, consentimiento y salud reproductiva, además de facilitar el acercamiento a recursos profesionales. Sin embargo, se observaron variaciones en la calidad informativa, predominio de testimonios no especializados, mitos sobre prevención del embarazo y riesgos vinculados a estereotipos y prácticas sexuales. Muchos estudios analizaron videos o poblaciones adultas, sin medir efectos causales en adolescentes. Se concluye que TikTok puede complementar, pero no sustituir, la educación sexual integral ni la consejería clínica. Desde enfermería se propone promover alfabetización mediática, verificación compartida, contenidos revisados y derivación oportuna, cuya efectividad deberá evaluarse en estudios específicos.

title: The Proximity Paradox: Unveiling the Hidden Costs of Familiarity in Hedge Fund Activism
journal: Journal of Applied Business and Economics
abstract: Geographical proximity can create familiarity that distorts investment decisions, even among sophisticated investors. This article reports results showing that activist hedge funds disproportionately target nearby firms and that these campaigns generate significantly lower returns, a pattern not explained by lower campaign costs or target selection effects. The article then develops a Strategic Target Evaluation Framework, a Decision-Making Toolkit, and a Training Module to help investment professionals identify and counteract familiarity bias. These tools promote geography-independent screening, disciplined due diligence, and structured decision-making to improve target selection and activism outcomes.

title: Self-medication prevalence patterns and behavioral drivers among undergraduate students in a semi-rural university community in Nigeria
abstract: Abstract Background Self-medication remains a significant public health concern in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), particularly among university populations where medicine accessibility, perceived knowledge, and healthcare barriers may encourage inappropriate medication use. Methods This descriptive cross-sectional study evaluated the prevalence, patterns, and behavioral drivers of self-medication in a semi-rural university–community setting in Ebonyi State, Nigeria. Participants comprised undergraduate students and the small number of eligible community pharmacists and patent and proprietary medicines vendors identified within the study setting. A stratified sampling approach was used, with random sampling among undergraduate students and census sampling among eligible community pharmacists and patent and proprietary medicines vendors. Of 228 participants invited, 224 provided complete responses, comprising 217 undergraduate students, 2 community pharmacists, and 5 patent and proprietary medicines vendors. Data were collected using a validated semi-structured questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics in SPSS version 26.0. The Health Belief Model provided the theoretical grounding for examining behavioral drivers of self-medication. Results Self-medication was reported at a moderate frequency (mean = 2.46/5). Headache or fever was the most commonly reported indication for self-treatment (mean = 3.79), followed by non-prescription use of pain relievers (mean = 3.46) and antimalarials (mean = 3.07). Non-prescription antibiotic use recorded a mean of 2.34. Behavioral drivers were also moderate (mean = 2.66), with the perception that illnesses were minor (mean = 3.42) and confidence in knowing which medicines worked (mean = 3.13) receiving the highest ratings. Respondents reported relatively low experience of adverse effects (mean = 1.78), although they recognized self-medication as a community health concern (mean = 3.22). Conclusion Among the predominantly undergraduate respondents, self-medication was associated more strongly with perceptions of illness severity and confidence in personal medication knowledge than with physical access barriers. The findings provide a context-specific baseline for a Health Belief Model-guided undergraduate intervention, while broader regulatory, counselling, healthcare-access, and antimicrobial-stewardship measures should be considered as complementary public health strategies.

title: Implementation of the Affordable Food Movement Policy in Support of Inflation Control in Palangka Raya City, Central Kalimantan Province
journal: International Journal of Economics, Management and Accounting (IJEMA)
abstract: Volatile food prices and heavy dependence on supplies from outside the region pose structural challenges to inflation control in Palangka Raya City. The city government runs the Affordable Food Movement (Gerakan Pangan Murah, GPM) as a direct market intervention, yet its effect on the official Consumer Price Index (CPI) remains limited. This descriptive qualitative case study analyzes why GPM has not controlled regional inflation optimally and formulates strategies to improve its implementation, using the Van Meter and Van Horn (1975) model. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with nine informant groups, observation, and document review, and verified through source and technique triangulation. Five inhibiting factors emerged: (1) a spatial mismatch between GPM sites and the BPS sample markets used for the CPI; (2) import dependence above 80% for volatile food across a vast, sparsely populated area; (3) the absence of a dedicated mayoral regulation and uncertain municipal funding; (4) limited human resources and the suspension of the mobile GPM fleet in 2026; and (5) short coordination lead times and uneven neighborhood-level socialization. Five strategies are proposed: aligning sites with sample markets, upstream inter-regional business-to-business cooperation, a mayoral regulation with earmarked budget, reactivating the mobile fleet with a task force, and a seven-day coordination SOP.

title: FUNGAL STUDY OF SPOILED BREAD HAWKED IN OKO
journal: International Journal of Organic and Medicinal Development Research
abstract: This study aimed in fungal assessment of spoiled bread hawked in Oko. The analysis was carried out with five different bread samples which were randomly purchased from different vendors at Oko and was aseptically sent to microbiology laboratory for fungal analysis, 1 gram of each of the sample were serially diluted and inoculated using the spread plate method after which it was incubated at 72-96 hours at 240C. The viable fungi colony count were 2 x 10-1cfu/g, 24.4 x 10-1 cfu/g, 13.4 x 10-1 cfu/g, 29.6 x 10-1 cfu/g and 26.4 x 10-1 cfu/g. The finding of this study showed that the colony forming unit did not exceed the National Agency for Food, Drug, Administration and Control (NAFDAC) standard of 103cfu/g. After the fungi analysis the probable organism gotten are Neurospora spp., Rizhopus spp, Conidiobolus spp, Aspergillus spp and Penicillum spp. Neurospora spp. was found to be the most occurring fungi in bread samples. It is recommended that measures as good hygiene in the bakeries and if necessary complementary post packaging heat treatments or modified atmosphere packaging is the best alternative.

title: Chemically induced hepatocyte-derived liver progenitors for liver disease: From laboratory research to clinical translation
abstract: Chemically induced hepatocyte-derived liver progenitors have emerged as a promising platform for liver regenerative medicine. In 2017, Katsuda et al. demonstrated that a combination of three small molecules—Y-27632, A-83-01, and CHIR99021—could convert mature rodent hepatocytes into proliferative, bipotent liver progenitor cells. Subsequent studies extended this concept to human hepatocytes using modified combinations of small molecules and growth factors, generating expandable progenitor populations with hepatic and biliary differentiation potential. Preclinical studies have demonstrated therapeutic effects of hepatocyte-derived liver progenitors in models of liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, acute liver injury, impaired regeneration, metabolic liver disease, and inherited metabolic disorders. Large-animal studies have further supported their feasibility and safety. More recently, a first-in-human study of human hepatocyte-derived liver progenitors in patients with cirrhosis demonstrated initial safety and feasibility, while an autologous clinical trial has entered recruitment in Japan. Further standardized and controlled clinical studies will be essential to establish the efficacy and long-term safety of these cells and to define their role in future liver regenerative therapies.

title: The value of evidence synthesis in animal science: a discussion and call to action
abstract: Abstract Population growth, climate change, and the advent of emerging infectious disease agents has put our abilities to feed the growing global population at risk. Despite considerable research investment to address this concern, there has been less attention to the development of robust methodologies for the synthesis of existing research evidence and its re-use. Evidence syntheses foster best practice, minimise wastage of research resources, and enable informed decision and policy making. In this call to action, some methodological development activities are proposed to increase the potential of evidence syntheses to tackle pressing societal issues relating to animal agriculture.
